messages:
mika: FYI discovered a CVE hit (tokenizers) that broke parts of the CI matrix this morning. flaky on macos wheels, passes on linux-manylinux. need triage and a short-term plan.

samir: can you paste the failing job log? is it an import error or a wheel build failure?

mika: import error during tests that exercise the C-extension fallback. snippet:

mika: ```
ImportError: cannot import name 'Tokenizers' from 'tokenizers' (unknown location)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/test_tokenizer_integration.py", line 12, in <module>
    from tokenizers import Tokenizer
ImportError: cannot import name 'Tokenizer' from 'tokenizers'
```

olivia: we saw this pattern last quarter — mac wheels mismatched manylinux ABI after a wheel rebuild upstream. vendor wheel tags differ. CI passes on linux because pip pulls manylinux wheel; mac picks wheel compiled on mac or falls back to source build and C-extension fails.

jordan: confirmed in the matrix: python3.10-macos-latest and py3.11-macos-latest fail, linux jobs ok. Repro steps: a simple venv, pip install tokenizers==0.13.3, run `python -c "import tokenizers"` fails.

samir: what's our current lock strategy? poetry.lock only? we have both pyproject/poetry and a constraints.txt used by our Docker builds.

mika: we use poetry.lock for dev and in CI we do `poetry export -f requirements.txt --dev` then pip install -r. No pinned abi tags.

olivia: short-term mitigation: pin tokenizers to the last known-good wheel release for macos in the matrix using a platform marker in the constraints file. Eg add to requirements: `tokenizers==0.13.2; sys_platform == "darwin"` or use `--platform` in pip for deterministic wheel selection. But that's brittle.

jordan: alternative: add a matrix-specific step to skip the test on macos until we patch upstream. Not ideal for security triage though — CVE present.

samir: CVE severity? Does the CVE allow remote code execution or is it denial-of-service? We need to categorize to prioritize.

mika: CVE-2026-XXXX (placeholder until advisory) shows memory corruption in the tokenizer C-ext when parsing malformed input. Repro PoC provided. High severity for ingestion endpoints that accept untrusted text.

olivia: given severity, we should aim for a patch in our dependency graph asap. Options:
- patch pin to a patched upstream (if available)
- backport upstream fix into a vendored wheel in our infra images
- add runtime mitigation: sanitize input lengths / reject certain byte sequences

jordan: upstream released 0.13.4rc with the fix but mac wheels not published yet. linux wheels published. So we can pin to 0.13.4 on linux and hold mac at 0.13.3 patched locally.

samir: propose surgical approach:
1) Add a constraints file `ci/constraints-macos.txt` with `tokenizers==0.13.4` once wheel exists, otherwise `tokenizers==0.13.3.postlocal` pointing to our internal wheel hash.
2) Build a mac wheel in our internal CI runner and upload to artifactory/our simple index.
3) Update poetry export step to `pip install --constraint ci/constraints-<platform>.txt -r requirements.txt`

mika: +1. For immediate blocker, I can build the mac wheel from upstream tag and publish to S3 simple index usable by CI. That will buy us time while upstream publishes official wheel.

olivia: checklist for release:
- [ ] reproduce PoC in a sandboxed runner
- [ ] publish internal wheel and update CI constraints
- [ ] run full matrix and smoke test canary route in staging
- [ ] open PR to regen poetry.lock to move to upstream 0.13.4 once mac wheel lands

samir: what's the CI change? can we keep it minimal? I suggest adding platform-aware constraint injection in the CI job template. Example in GitHub Actions:

samir: ```yaml
- name: Export requirements
  run: poetry export -f requirements.txt --dev --without-hashes > requirements.txt
- name: Install deps with platform constraints
  run: |
    if [[ $RUNNER_OS == 'macOS' ]]; then cp ci/constraints-macos.txt constraints.txt; else cp ci/constraints-linux.txt constraints.txt; fi
    pip install -r requirements.txt -c constraints.txt
```

jordan: CI-bot: triggered matrix rerun on the failing branch w/ a patched wheel from mika's artifact host.

ci-bot: Re-run queued. Jobs 12/12 started.

mika: deployed internal wheel -> tests pass locally on macos VM. Pushing artifact link to thread.

mika: link: https://internal-artifacts.redwood.local/simple/tokenizers/0.13.3.postlocal/tokenizers-0.13.3.postlocal-cp310-macosx.whl

olivia: agreed to land the temporary CI constraints PR (small change, annotated with CVE and expiry). We'll set an expiry tag to remind to revert once upstream has official mac wheel.

samir: long-term: add audit signal to detect platform-specific wheel mismatches. Also add a check in the dep-scan job to verify identical hashes across platform wheels when upstream publishes a release; alert if mac wheel missing.

jordan: also open a ticket for KMS/audit traces: when we publish internal wheel we need to record who created the artifact and sign it. That integrates with compliance requirements for Private deployments.

mika: created ticket INF-1439: "internal wheel publish + signing + audit log for emergency dependency patches" and assigned to samir.

samir: I'm taking INF-1439. ETA EOD tomorrow for initial airflow to record S3 put events and signatures. We'll use existing KMS key and log via our audit pipeline.

olivia: follow-up: we'll schedule a canary rollout for pinned change to a small dedicated pool to monitor regressions on latency and memory.

jordan: final decision: land constraint PR as hotfix, publish internal wheel, run full matrix, and open regen PR for poetry.lock to adopt upstream 0.13.4 when mac wheel published. Document mitigation steps in the CVE tracker.

mika: I'll open the PR for the CI constraint now and link to the artifact and PoC. tagging @samir @olivia @jordan for review :thumbsup:

samir: thanks, let's keep this thread for status. I'll comment on INF-1439 with the audit design.

devsec-bot: CVE-2026-XXXX severity marked HIGH. Advisory ticket created: sec-8721. Notifying product/incident channels.

mika: noted. will post status in #incidents if we escalate to broader customer notification.

olivia: important: add a brief note in our release notes and customer incident if we need to rotate keys or touch Private deployments. For now it's just dependency patching.

jordan: good work team. once PR lands I'll merge and monitor staging metrics.

mika: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-platform/pull/789 (hotfix/constraints-macos)

samir: LGTM, approving now.

ci-bot: All checks passed on PR 789 after internal wheel injection.

mika: merging now.

olivia: after merge, let's schedule a follow-up in #eng-sre tomorrow to validate canary. closing thread in a bit.

mika: closing after canary green. thanks all.
